Business Analytics and Applied AI Minor
programs.changeNote: Considering evolving technology trends and the growing importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in business, we propose revising the existing Business Analytics (BA) Minor into the new "Business Analytics and Applied AI" minor.  This revision ensures students gain essential exposure to AI while maintaining strong foundations in analytics. Peer institutions and industry demand emphasize AI and analytics as core competencies, and aligning our program with these trends will strengthen its market relevance and student appeal.  This has been strongly affirmed through consultation with the ASB Alumni Advisory Board and other industry professionals.  The proposed change involves a modest adjustment by rearranging existing approved courses. Specifically, INFO 345 (AI for Business) would move into the core curriculum to ensure every student completes an AI-focused course, while INFO 311 (Business Analytics II) would move into the elective pool. This ensures that all students gain direct exposure to AI in business decision-making, while maintaining the flexibility for students who wish to pursue more advanced analytics topics. The revision strengthens the program’s marketability, aligns with Ramapo priorities in technology and innovation, and enhances student preparation for data-driven decision making.

programs.name: Computer Science Minor
programs.changeNote: This proposal revises the Computer Science minor to reduce the total requirement from six courses to five courses, and to allow students flexibility in choosing either the C++ programming sequence (CMPS 147/148/231) or the Python programming sequence (CMPS 130/240) as their foundation. These changes make the minor more accessible to students outside the traditional computing majors while preserving rigorous preparation in computer science fundamentals.This proposal revises the Computer Science minor to reduce the total requirement from six courses to five courses, and to allow students flexibility in choosing either the C++ programming sequence (CMPS 147/148/231) or the Python programming sequence (CMPS 130/240) as their foundation. These changes make the minor more accessible to students outside the traditional computing majors while preserving rigorous preparation in computer science fundamentals.  The current Computer Science minor requires six courses:  CMPS 147 – Computer Science I (C++) CMPS 148 – Computer Science II (C++) CMPS 231 – Data Structures Three CMPS electives (at least two at the 300-level)  The original rationale for requiring the C++ sequence (CMPS 147/148/231) was that students needed these courses as prerequisites for upper-level electives. This is no longer the case. The Python sequence (CMPS 130/240) now provides sufficient preparation for several upper-level courses including CMPS 305 (Cyber Security), CMPS 310 (Big Data Programming), CMPS 331 (Artificial Intelligence), CMPS 364 (Database Design), CMPS 369 (Web Application Development), and CMPS 370 (Cyber and Network Defense). This pathway is already used by Data Science and Bioinformatics majors who successfully complete these upper-level courses.Several factors motivate this revision: Limited enrollment from outside computing disciplines. The current minor has not attracted students from outside Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or Mathematics. Current enrollment consists of nine students, all from Cybersecurity or Data Science programs. No major conversions. The minor has not converted students to the Computer Science major in the past five years, indicating it is not serving as a pipeline to the major. Course length. At six courses, the current minor is larger than typical minors across the college. Reducing to five courses aligns with standard minor expectations. Enrollment pressures. Attracting students from other majors into our courses supports healthy enrollment across the CMPS curriculum.

Interdisciplinary Studies BA
programs.changeNote: This program revision/update is designed to actively embrace and celebrate cross-disciplinary study.  A single, College-wide independent/flexible design major serves multiple purposes: Provides maximum flexibility within a structure that ensures academic rigor and a commitment to interdisciplinarity; Enables Ramapo to actively promote it as an option to prospective students; Meets the different needs of multiple student populations simultaneously; Actively encourages students to utilize courses from throughout the Ramapo curriculum; Positions Ramapo as a place that welcomes learners at all stages of their academic careers. This major leads to a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree.
